Below is a quick, step‑by‑step guide to let users sign in to your Supabase app **just with an email address** (no password). You’ll configure this on the Supabase console and then add a tiny bit of code to your front‑end (or back‑end if you prefer). --- ## 1. Enable “Magic link” (passwordless) in the Supabase Console | Step | What to do | Screenshot? | |------|------------|--------------| | 1️⃣ | Log into the Supabase web console at https://app.supabase.com and open the project you’re working on. | – | | 2️⃣ | Go to **Auth → Settings → External OAuth** (or simply **Auth → Settings**). | – | | 3️⃣ | Under **Email login**, enable **“Allow magic link only”**. This does two things: - Turns on email‑only sign‑in via a magic link sent to the user’s inbox. - Disables the standard password/credential flow. | – | | 4️⃣ | Save your changes. The console will now show **Passwordless** as the active method. | – | > **Tip:** If you want to *also* allow password‑based logins in addition to magic links, simply leave the switch “Allow passwordless only” **off**. For a pure “no‑password” experience, keep it on. --- ## 2. (Optional) Configure Email Provider If you’re using Supabase’s built‑in “Mail” for magic links, it will use the default settings (which works for most projects). For production or custom branding: | Step | What to do | |------|------------| | 1️⃣ | In **Auth → Settings → Email‑auth**, set your **SMTP provider** (SendGrid, Mailgun, etc.). | | 2️⃣ | Set **From Email** and **From Name** to the values you want in the sender field. | | 3️⃣ | Optionally edit the **Magic link URL** (the default is `https://your-project.supabase.co/auth/v1/verify`). | --- ## 3. Add the Front‑End Code Below are minimal examples for the most common frameworks. Replace `YOUR_SUPABASE_URL` and `YOUR_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` with the values from your project settings. ### 3.1 JavaScript / TypeScript (plain) ```html ``` > `signInWithOtp` is the newest Supabase function that covers both magic links and phone‑code sign‑ins. For email‑only, you pass `{ email }`. ### 3.2 React (using the `@supabase/auth-helpers-react`) ```bash npm i @supabase/auth-helpers-react @supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs ``` ```tsx // EmailLogin.tsx import { useSupabaseClient } from '@supabase/auth-helpers-react'; import { useState } from 'react'; export default function EmailLogin() { const supabase = useSupabaseClient(); const [email, setEmail] = useState(''); const sendMagicLink = async () => { const { error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ email }); if (error) console.error(error.message); else alert('Magic link sent!'); }; return (
setEmail(e.target.value)} placeholder="you@example.com"/>

The call pattern is the same: ```swift // Swift supabaseClient.auth.signIn(withOtp: .email(email: "you@example.com")) ``` ```kotlin // Kotlin val auth = supabaseClient.auth auth.signInWithOtp(SignInWithOtpRequest(email = "you@example.com")) ``` --- ## 4. Handle the Redirect When the user clicks the magic link, Supabase redirects them back to the URL you set in **Auth → Settings → Redirect URLs**. Typically you’ll have a “/auth/callback” route that finishes the session: ```ts // Next.js example import { useEffect } from 'react' import { useRouter } from 'next/router' import { supabase } from '../lib/initSupabase' export default function SignInCallback() { const router = useRouter() useEffect(() => { supabase.auth .getSession() .then(() => router.push('/')) // redirect to home after sign‑in .catch(err => console.error(err)) }, []) return
Signing you in...
} ``` --- ## 5. Verify Everything Works 1. Open your app → click “Sign In.” 2. Enter an email → you should receive an email with an embedded link. 3. Click the link → you’re logged in and redirected to your app. If the email never arrives: - Check the **Email logs** under **Auth → Logs**. - Verify your SMTP settings or use the free Supabase “Mail” if you’re in dev mode. --- ## 6. Optional: Store Extra User Data When a user signs in for the first time, Supabase automatically creates a row in `auth.users`. If you need to add more info (like a display name): ```ts const { data, error } = await supabase .from('profiles') .insert([{ id: user.id, full_name: '' }]) ``` You can hook this into the auth callback so that each new user gets a profile row immediately. --- ## 7
